As clarified in the sūtras,
I shall now briefly describe its characteristics.
This hell is surrounded on all sides by seven layers of iron walls.
Furthermore, seven layers of iron nets cover its top,
and below are seven layers of iron blades forming a forest.
Immeasurable fierce fires, eighty-four thousand yojanas in length and breadth, rage there.
The bodies of the sinners fill the entire space within it;
yet, due to the conditions of their karmic offenses, they do not obstruct one another.
The upper fires penetrate downward, and the lower fires penetrate upward.
It penetrates and interconnects through the east, west, south, and north;
like a fish on a griddle whose fat and grease are entirely consumed,
the suffering of sin within this place is likewise so.
At its four gates there are four great bronze dogs.
Their bodies are four thousand yojanas in length and breadth;
their fangs and claws are sharp and long, and their eyes are like flashing lightning.
Furthermore, there are immeasurable birds with iron beaks that soar and fly about, devouring the flesh of the sinners;
the ox-headed hell-wardens resemble rākṣasas and have nine tails.
Its tail was like an iron trident,
and it had nine heads,
with eighteen horns upon each head.
Each horn has sixty-four eyes,
and from every single eye there burst forth glowing iron balls that burn the flesh of the sinners;
moreover, when it bellows in a fit of wrath and fury, its voice is like a thunderclap.
Furthermore, immeasurable and boundless wheels of swords descend through the air;
they enter through the crowns of the sinners' heads and emerge from their feet.
Thereupon, the pain of these sinners penetrates to the very marrow of their bones, cutting into their livers and hearts with excruciating intensity.
Thus, for innumerable years, they sought life but could not find it, and sought death but could not find it.
For such retributions as these, we today all bow our heads in shame and repentance.
Next, I further repent for the retribution of having my body and head severed upon the mountains of blades and the forests of swords in hell;
I repent for the retribution of being burned and boiled in the cauldrons of boiling water and the furnaces of glowing coals in hell.
I repent for the retributive offenses of the burning iron beds and copper pillars in hell;
I repent for the retributive offenses of being split and crushed by the wheel-blades and flaming chariots in hell;
I repent for the retributive offenses of the agonizing pain of having the tongue pulled out and being plowed over in hell.
I repent for the retribution of the hell of swallowing iron balls and having molten copper poured into one's mouth, wherein the five internal organs are consumed and rotted away.
I repent for the retribution of the hell of being ground by iron, wherein the bones and flesh are reduced to dust and powder.
I repent for the retribution of the Black Rope Hell, where the limbs and joints are torn asunder.
I repent for the retribution of the Ash River and Boiling Excrement Hells, where one suffers from distress and suffocation.
I repent for the retribution of the Brine and Cold Ice Hells, where the skin is split open and one is naked and frozen.
I repent for the retribution of the crimes of mutual slaughter and injury committed in the hells of jackals, wolves, hawks, and dogs;
I repent for the retribution of the crimes of mutual grappling, seizing, hacking, and stabbing committed in the hell of weapons, talons, and claws.
Repent of the retribution for the sin of being roasted on spits in the Fire Pit Hell;
repent of the retribution for the sin of having one's body shattered by two colliding rocks in the Hell of Two Stones;
repent of the retribution for the sin of being dismembered in the Black-Eared Assembly Hell.
I repent for the retribution of being hacked and minced in the Dark Meat Mountain Hell;
I repent for the retribution of being sawn apart and nailed to the body in the Hell of Saws and Nails;
I repent for the retribution of being butchered and sliced while suspended upside down with iron clubs in the Hell of Iron Clubs.
I repent for the retribution of the grievous sins that lead to rebirth in the scorching and howling hells;
I repent for the retribution of the long, dark nights between the Great and Small Iron Ring Mountains where one does not recognize the three luminaries.
I repent of the Āpapa hell, the Apapā hell, and the Aṭaṭa hell.
The Āraḍa hell. Thus, within all eight cold and eight hot hells,
there are further eighty-four thousand subsidiary *kalala* (enclosed) hells as their retinue.
Within this, there are the tortures of being roasted and boiled in the fires of sin;
the immeasurable sufferings of having one's skin flayed, flesh scraped away, bones pared down, marrow beaten out, intestines pulled, and lungs extracted—
sufferings that cannot be heard and cannot be described.
Homage to the Buddha! Those who are here within this place today may be our parents from beginningless births or all our kinsmen and relatives.
After they have passed away, we—
Or they may fall once again into such a hell.

Today, with a purified mind, I pray fervently, prostrating myself with my forehead to the ground before the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Bodhisattvas of the great earth, seeking their compassion and repenting.
May all these retributions for sins be utterly extinguished.
By virtue of the merit arising from this confession of the retributions of the hells and so forth,
may they be destroyed this very instant.
The Iron City of Avīci was entirely transformed into a Pure Land, where even the name of the evil realms no longer existed.
All the instruments of suffering in the other hells were converted into conditions of bliss,
and the mountains of blades and sword-trees became groves of precious jewels.
Those in the boiling cauldrons and the glowing coals are reborn through transformation within lotus flowers;
the ox-headed hell-wardens abandon their cruelty and violence,
all giving rise to compassion and harboring no evil thoughts.
The sentient beings in the hells attain liberation from the fruits of suffering and no longer create its causes;
they experience equal peace and happiness as if in the third dhyāna.
At that time, they all simultaneously gave rise to the aspiration for the unsurpassed Way.
Having finished their repentance,
they with sincere hearts took refuge in and paid homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.

Homage to Vairocana Buddha. Homage to our Original Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha. Homage to Amitābha Buddha. Homage to Maitreya Buddha. Homage to Nāgottamarāja Buddha. Homage to Nāgeśvararāja Buddha. Homage to Ratnaśrī Buddha. Homage to Bodhimaṇḍala-vyūheśvararāja Buddha. Homage to Kāṣāyadhvaja Buddha. Homage to Siṃhanāda Buddha. Homage to Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva. Homage to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Homage to Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva. Homage to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. Homage to Mahāvyūha Bodhisattva. Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Having paid homage to all the Buddhas, [I take refuge].
Next, perform repentance again.
Having already completed the repentance for the retribution of the hells,
one should now, in turn, repent for the retribution of the three evil realms.
In the sutra, the Buddha said:
"Because those with many desires seek much profit,
their suffering and affliction are also many."
One who is content, though lying upon the ground,
still considers it happiness;
one who lacks contentment, though dwelling in heaven, still finds no satisfaction.
Yet when people of the world suddenly encounter urgent distress,
they are able to relinquish their wealth regardless of its amount;
they do not realize, however, that this body stands upon the edge of a deep pit leading to the three miserable realms.
If one does not return even for a single breath, one will immediately fall [into the lower realms].
Suddenly, a spiritual friend exhorted him to cultivate meritorious deeds,
causing him to practice the provisions for wholesome dharmas in the future.
To cling to this stingy mind and refuse to act accordingly is the height of folly and delusion. Why is this so?
In the Sūtra, the Buddha said:
"At the time of birth, one does not bring even a single coin;
at the time of death, one likewise departs without carrying even a single coin."
One undergoes physical suffering and accumulates [merit] for its sake, yet this leads only to anxiety and distress.
It benefits oneself not at all but serves only the interests of others;
there is no goodness upon which to rely, nor any virtue to depend on.
Consequently, at the end of their lives, they fall into the various evil realms.
For this reason, today we take refuge in the Triple Gem and perform sincere repentance.
Next, one further repents of the retribution for the lack of discernment within the animal realm;
one repents of the retribution for the burden of carrying heavy loads and pulling plows to repay past debts within the animal realm.
I repent for the karmic retribution of being unable to attain mastery within the realm of animals,
and for the offenses of being hacked, pierced, slaughtered, and dismembered by others.
I repent for the karmic retribution of having no feet, two feet, four feet, or many feet within the realm of animals.
I repent for the retribution of my sins incurred while in the bodies of animals within the realm of beasts— specifically,
the sin of being devoured by various small insects from within their feathers, fur, scales,
and shells. Such are the immeasurable karmic retributions found within the realm of animals.
Today, with utmost sincerity, we repent all of this.
Next, we further repent for having long endured hunger and thirst within the realm of hungry ghosts for hundreds of thousands of myriads of years,
never once hearing even the name of water or grain as retribution for our sins.
I repent for the retribution of the hungry ghosts who consume pus, blood, excrement, and filth;
I repent for the retribution of the hungry ghosts whose every limb and joint blazes with fire whenever they move their bodies.
I repent for the retribution of the crime of having a belly as vast as that of a hungry ghost while possessing a throat as narrow as a needle.
Thus, all the immeasurable sufferings within the realm of hungry ghosts,
I now prostrate myself in sorrowful supplication and repent for them all.
Next, one further repents of the retributive offenses of flattery, arrogance, and deceit committed within the realms of all ghosts, spirits, and asuras.
One repents of the retributive offenses of carrying sand and bearing stones to fill rivers and dam up seas committed within the realm of ghosts and spirits.
I repent for the various evil spirits, such as ghosts, deities, rākṣasas, and kumbhāṇḍas, who devour blood and flesh at birth and undergo this wretched retribution of ugliness;
likewise, I repent for all the immeasurable and boundless retributions of sin within the realm of ghosts and spirits.
Today, with my head bowed in prostration toward the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Bodhisattvas of the great earth,
I seek compassion and repent, praying that all [obstacles] be completely extinguished.
May the merit arising from this repentance for the retribution of animal births and the like be fully realized.
May I, in life after life, extinguish the defilement of ignorance;
may I personally recognize the conditions of karma so that wisdom shines brightly, severing the body of the evil realms.
By means of the merit produced through this repentance, may the retributions of hungry ghosts and the like be extinguished.
May they, in life after life, forever be free from the suffering of stinginess, greed, hunger, and thirst;
may they always partake of the nectar-like flavor of liberation.
By virtue of the merit generated through this repentance for [the offenses of] ghosts, spirits, and asuras, may these vows be fulfilled.
May they be upright and sincere in life after life, free from flattery;
may they abandon the causes of wrong livelihood and eliminate the fruits of ugliness,
thereby bringing benefit and merit to humans and devas.
From this moment until I reach the site of enlightenment,
may I resolutely never undergo the retribution of the four evil realms of existence,
except for when I manifest there out of great compassion for the sake of sentient beings.
By the power of their vows, they remain therein without weariness.
Having already repented for the retributions of the three miserable realms,
we shall now once again prostrate ourselves in earnest repentance for the remaining karmic retributions within the human and celestial realms.
We all receive this lifespan of Jambudvīpa;
yet, though it is said to last a hundred years, those who complete it are few indeed.
Within that interval, many meet with premature death in the prime of their youth.
Their number is immeasurable.
They are pursued by manifold sufferings that torment both mind and body; they are beset by grief, anxiety, fear, and dread, never for a moment free from them.
All this is because their roots of goodness are feeble while their evil karma is vast and abundant.
Consequently, whatever one does in the present does not accord with one's wishes;
one should know that all of this is the residual retribution of evil karma from the past.
Therefore, [I], such-and-such a person, now perform repentance for everything from beginningless time until this day.
I repent for all remaining karmic retributions among humans and devas in the present and the future;
I repent for the calamities and karmic debts from past lives that afflict humanity,
and for the retributive offenses of the hundred ailments and the impairment of the six sense faculties.
I repent for the retributive offenses of holding wrong views in the borderlands of the human realm and the karmic results of the three evil paths and eight difficulties.
I repent for the retributive offenses of being frequently ill and emaciated in the human realm, and the karmic results of a shortened lifespan and untimely death.
I repent for the karmic retribution of being unable to maintain constant harmony and protection among one's six types of human relatives and kin.
I repent for the karmic retribution of the suffering of separation from loved ones due to the decline and death of human friends and associates.
I repent for the retribution of offenses that cause the gathering of human enemies amidst grief, sorrow, fear, and dread.
I repent for the retribution of offenses that cause the perils and terrors of water, fire, bandits, and weapons, leading to danger, alarm, and cowardice.
I repent for the karmic retribution of being solitary, suffering, and wandering in exile among humans, having lost one’s kingdom and territory;
I repent for the karmic retribution of being imprisoned and confined in human jails, subjected to shackles and fetters, and tortured with whips and cudgels.
I repent for the karmic retribution of human disputes, both public and private,
involving mutual entanglement and slander;
I repent for the karmic retribution of malignant illnesses that persist for years and months without healing, leaving one bedridden and unable to rise or move.
I repent for the karmic retribution of winter epidemics, summer pestilences, and the injuries of contagious fevers among human beings.
I repent for the karmic retribution of malignant winds, swellings, and obstructions among human beings.
I repent for the karmic retribution of being sought out by various evil spirits who watch for an opportunity to inflict calamities and misfortunes upon human beings.
I repent for the karmic retribution of performing sorcery and strange anomalies among humans by means of bird cries, the hundred monsters, flying corpses, and malevolent ghosts.
I repent for the karmic retribution of being harmed among humans by tigers, leopards, jackals, wolves, and all manner of evil beasts of water and land.
I repent for the karmic retribution of committing suicide by hanging oneself among humans;
I repent for the karmic retribution of throwing oneself into pits, leaping into fire, drowning oneself, or falling off cliffs among humans;
I repent for the karmic retribution of lacking majesty, virtue, and renown among humans.
I repent for the retribution of my sins regarding the failure of human clothing and the necessities of life to accord with one's heart’s desires.

I repent for the retribution of my sins regarding the obstacles created by encountering evil associates (pāpa-mitra) during my movements, comings and goings, and various activities in the human world.
Thus, regarding the immeasurable calamities, misfortunes, epidemics, hardships, afflictions, and karmic retributions that exist among humans and devas in the present and the future,
we, [Name] and others, today with utmost sincerity, seek compassionate repentance before the Buddhas of the ten directions, the Honored Dharma, and the Noble Assembly.
May they all be extinguished.
Previously, I have already repented of all afflictive hindrances and all karmic hindrances pertaining to the three karmas and six sense faculties.
Regarding all karmic obstacles of retribution within the four modes of birth and the six realms of existence,

we shall now successively make vows and dedicate the merit arising from this repentance of the three obstacles. May those of us, such-and-such, by means of this merit produced through the repentance of the three obstacles, [attain...]
I dedicate it all in its entirety to bestow upon all sentient beings.
Together with them, I repent and vow that all sentient beings may experience peace and happiness of body and mind within their present lives.
All inauspicious events, such as the three calamities and the eight difficulties, shall be entirely eliminated;
food and clothing will be abundant,
and one shall possess right faith in the Triple Gem.
Upon casting off this retribution body, they shall all attain rebirth in the World of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*).
There they will personally attend upon Amitābha and receive the prediction of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*).
In a future age, they will behold Maitreya Buddha.
May I hear the true Dharma and practice accordingly as taught.
Furthermore, may I, in every birth and in every place throughout all lifetimes,
always encounter kings who cause the Triple Gem to flourish.
May I not be born into the families of external paths or those with false views.
Furthermore, may I, in birth after birth and in every place throughout all lifetimes,
be born by transformation within a lotus flower into a lineage that is noble and preeminent.
May there be peace, security, and happiness, with clothing and food provided spontaneously. Furthermore, may I,
in birth after birth and in every place throughout all lifetimes,
possess a mind of loving-kindness, benevolence, loyalty, and filial piety, and equally assist all beings.
May I not give rise to even a single thought of hostility or harm.
Furthermore, may I, in every birth and throughout all lifetimes, in every place and at every moment,
always be protected and remembered by all Buddhas.
They are able to subdue the hosts of Māra and all non-Buddhists;
they assemble together with all bodhisattvas in one place,
and their resolve for the path to enlightenment continues in succession without interruption.
Furthermore, I vow that in every birth, life after life, and in every place, wherever I may be,
I shall cause the Buddha-dharma to flourish and manifest, practice the Mahāyāna,
and emanate infinite bodies to rescue and deliver all sentient beings.
Until reaching the site of enlightenment without ever regressing,
may I fulfill the vows made by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
as well as the merit, wisdom, and dedications they have cultivated and practiced.
I am also like this:
I make the vow to cultivate and accumulate [merit] until the realm of empty space is exhausted and the realm of sentient beings is exhausted.
While the karma and afflictions of sentient beings may come to an end, this dedication of my practice shall never be exhausted.
Having made this vow and dedication,
I reverently pay homage with a sincere heart to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
